importantNotes: Jesus referenced Jonah as a sign — three days in the fish paralleling three days in the tomb (Matt 12:40).
The book teaches that God's compassion extends to all people, even Israel's enemies.
Nineveh was the capital of Assyria — Israel's greatest enemy.
Jonah is the only prophet in the OT whose audience (the Ninevites) actually repented.
The real lesson is not the fish — it's about God's heart for all nations.

chapters.1: God calls Jonah to preach to Nineveh; Jonah flees by ship; a great storm; Jonah is thrown overboard.
chapters.2: Jonah prays from inside the great fish; God commands the fish to vomit him onto dry land.
chapters.3: Jonah preaches to Nineveh; the entire city repents and God relents from judgment.
chapters.4: Jonah is angry that God showed mercy; God teaches him about compassion through a vine.
